pattern.top_pattern: VA CSNP acute hospital growth is broad, with added provider-level cost pressure
pattern.what_is_impacting: VA CSNP HMO acute hospital inpatient spend with prior authorization
pattern.pattern_details: VA CSNP acute hospital spend increased through a combination of broader admission growth and added provider-level cost pressure. The broad market signal shows more inpatient use, while specific hospitals show higher paid per admit. The action should combine admission management with targeted hospital performance review.
pattern.why_it_matters: This extends the VA inpatient pressure beyond DSNP and suggests a wider SNP hospital-management issue in the market.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Expand the VA inpatient response beyond DSNP by reviewing CSNP admission drivers and hospital-specific pricing or severity patterns at VCU, Riverside, Sentara Leigh, and Sentara Norfolk.
evidence_summary: VA CSNP HMO acute hospital signals total about $8.4M.
Broad utilization added about $6.5M with 481 more admissions while paid per admit fell about $2.3K.
Separate provider-level pressure at Sentara Leigh Hospital and Sentara Norfolk General Hospital added about $1.9M with higher paid per admit.
